unsupported on the agent's OS.

Response shape:

    "agent_id": str,
    "framework": str,
    "summary": {"eligible": int, "blocked": int, "unsupported": int},
    "eligible":    [{name, description, emoji, source, homepage}],
    "blocked":     [{name, description, emoji, missing: {bins, env}}],

delete.description:
Permanently and fully delete the user's account.

Deletes every agent row, cancels any Stripe subscription, removes all
user-owned records (wallet ledger + enterprise account, API keys,
projects, LLM usage, Stripe billing links, webhook subs,
sessions, notifications, usage/trace events), and deletes the NextAuth
login identity (User/Account/Session) so the account is truly gone, not
just its agents. Runtime teardown (containers/VMs/volumes/networks, plus
the Inkbox identity for identity-framework agents) runs as background
tasks after the response, via the same cleanup path single-agent deletes
use. A confirmation email goes to the (pre-captured) address once the
login identity is verified gone.

Every step runs in its own SAVEPOINT. Postgres aborts the *entire*
transaction on any failed statement, so the previous version (which issued
`DELETE FROM customers …` against a table that doesn't exist on this
deployment) poisoned the transaction and silently rolled back the whole
deletion (including the agents), then 500'd. Savepoints isolate each step so
one failure can't undo the rest.

patch.description:
Turn the screen capability on/off for an existing agent (owner only).

Enabling re-runs the per-plan desktop cap for seats accounts (402 with
code=seat_limit, same shape as create). The flag only changes what the
NEXT boot does: MARITIME_DESKTOP=1 lands in the injected env, maritime-init
launches the desktop stack, and fc-manager's rebase-on-wake cold-boots a
snapshot that lacks the desktop drive (plan 33 B).

There is no persisted "recreate on next wake" marker in the wake path —
wake only recreates when a snapshot is genuinely unusable (plan 30 A1),
and image/env changes take effect on the next restart. So this applies
the change exactly the way env-var edits do (routers/agents.py skill
env): an ACTIVE agent is rebooted through orchestrator.restart_agent
(stop -> commit derived rootfs -> recreate with fresh env); a sleeping or
stopped agent keeps its snapshot and the change lands on its next
restart/cold boot, surfaced as requiresRestart=true. Enabling also
raises the agent's RAM/CPU floor to the desktop default (4 GiB / 2 vCPU)
when it is below — a 2 GB VM runs the screen with ~300 MB free, which is
one Chromium tab away from OOM. Larger allocations are left alone;
disabling never shrinks (use the resize endpoint).

with shell quoting) or a raw shell string. stdout/stderr come back merged,
because Firecracker's command server returns a single stream, and the exit
code is recovered via a sentinel because not every runtime reports one.

Push a text message to the user's Telegram chat for this agent.

Body: `{"text": "..."}`. Returns 200 with the chat_id on success,
401 if the bearer doesn't HMAC-match the agent_id, 404 if the
agent has no Telegram binding, 503 if the shared bot isn't
configured for this deployment.

Open a Browserbase Live View session for the agent and DM the
user the URL via Telegram (optionally) so the user can interactively
log in to a third-party site.

Works for both Maritime-pool agents AND agents with user-supplied
BROWSERBASE_API_KEY + BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID. For BYO-key agents,
the session is created under the user's own Browserbase account
so cookies set during the takeover persist into the agent's later
MCP sessions.

Body (all optional): `{"service": "facebook"}`, a descriptor used in
the DM text. No state-tracking; session lives ~10 min on Browserbase's
side, then auto-expires.

Returns 200 with `{session_id, live_view_url, expires_at, telegram_delivered}`.
Errors:
  - 401: bad/missing internal token
  - 404: agent not found
  - 503: agent has no Browserbase credentials (no BYO key AND no pool)
  - 502: Browserbase API call failed

End a Live View session early once the agent confirms login worked.

Body: `{"session_id": "..."}`. Idempotent: already-closed/expired
sessions return 200. Cookies set during the session are persisted to
the agent's Context regardless of whether we explicitly close it
(Browserbase's 600s timeout takes care of orphans).

Record a Browserbase session that was opened by the
@browserbasehq/mcp server (i.e. the agent called a browser tool,
not the explicit `maritime-request-login` flow).

Called by the maritime-bb-mcp-wrap shell wrapper around the bb-mcp
binary, which tails stderr for the SessionManager's
"Browserbase Live Debugger URL: .../sessions/<id>" line and POSTs
each session id here. Inserts a `browser_sessions` row so the
dashboard's Live Browser panel (which polls
`/api/agents/{id}/browser/live-view` and reads from that table)
auto-expands for MCP-driven browsing, not only for the
`maritime-request-login` path.

Idempotent: `record_session_start` no-ops on duplicate session_id,
so retries (wrapper restart, transient curl error) don't
double-count.

Session billing close still goes through `get_live_view`'s lazy
reap (which marks `ended_at` but does NOT call `bill_session_close`,
the same gap as the request-login path; tracked separately).

Tier C schedule push (plan 24 phase 3): the agent (via the SDK's
observeScheduler wrap, or plain curl) POSTs a read-only projection of
its own scheduler the moment it changes:

    {"schedules": [{"id": ..., "nextRunAt"?: ISO, "cron"?: "5-field",
                    "tz"?: IANA, "prompt"?: str, "name"?: str}, ...]}

The list is reconciled AUTHORITATIVELY through the same byo_sync
provider the Tier B GET /schedules poll uses, so push and poll can
never fight: sending the full current list adds, updates, and
garbage-collects in one call. An empty list clears all synced wakes.

Returns {"upserted": n, "deleted": n, "desired": n}.

Mint the OAuth authorize URL + DM it to the user via Telegram.

Configure auto-recharge: below thresholdCents, charge the saved card
for amountCents (max 3x/24h, 6h backoff after a failed charge).

Enabling requires a saved card RIGHT NOW (2026-07-17 decision): an
opt-in that cannot charge is worse than none, because the user believes
refills are armed while the sweep fails forever. Callers get a 400 with
a machine-readable `code` (SDKs wrap this endpoint). Disabling is never
blocked. The check is skipped only when Stripe itself is unconfigured
(dev environments, where the sweep could not charge anyway).

the UI can warn when auto-recharge has nothing workable to bill. Read
only: never creates a Stripe customer, and the Stripe lookups run in a
worker thread so a slow Stripe API cannot stall the event loop on every
/billing page load.

Shapes: {hasCard: true, brand, last4, expMonth, expYear, expired} or
{hasCard: false, reason: not_configured|no_customer|no_card|stripe_error}.
The UI treats stripe_error/not_configured as unknown, not as missing.

The AI credits of the account: budget, lifetime spend, what is left,
and the unexpired welcome credit (``welcomeCredit``, None once spent or
lapsed).

Browser session usage + rate for the authenticated user.

Sessions are debited from the same wallet as hosting compute (see
`services/browserbase_pool.bill_session_close`), at
`settings.browserbase_rate_per_hour_cents`. Only pooled sessions
(Maritime-supplied Browserbase) are billed. User-key sessions
return `cost_cents = 0`.

post.description:
Creates a Stripe Checkout session that buys AI credits.

The session is a one-time payment on the account's Stripe customer.
``invoice_creation`` is on so the purchase produces a Stripe invoice
(receipt PDF in the portal, a row in the invoice history), tagged
``type=ai_credits`` like the Checkout session itself. The webhook for
``checkout.session.completed`` raises the budget; the invoice events
for this invoice match no billing engine and only sync the receipt.

One-time $10 OpenClaw signup bonus. Idempotent: replays return the
existing balance without double-crediting.

Amount is server-controlled (SIGNUP_BONUS_CENTS); the caller has no input
beyond their authenticated identity. Replaces the legacy pattern of having
the frontend call /api/wallet/credit directly (AUTH-002).

credit buys nothing on seats, so minting it is pure ledger noise — but
the response MUST stay 200 because the openclaw deploy flow
(frontend /api/openclaw/deploy) treats any non-ok here as fatal and
aborts the whole signup.
